purpose: Pseudoephedrine is used to relieve a stuffy or congested nose caused by colds, allergies, or sinus problems. It helps you breathe more easily by reducing the swelling and congestion in your nasal passages. It is a short-term relief medicine, not a cure for the underlying condition.
how_it_works: Pseudoephedrine works by tightening up the blood vessels in the lining of your nose and sinuses. When those blood vessels shrink, the swollen tissue goes down and air can flow through more easily. Think of it like squeezing a sponge — it reduces the puffiness that is blocking your airflow.
common_side_effects: Feeling nervous, restless, or jittery; trouble sleeping especially if taken too late in the day; faster heartbeat; increased blood pressure; headache; dizziness; dry mouth; and decreased appetite.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you have high blood pressure, heart disease, an enlarged prostate, thyroid problems, diabetes, or glaucoma without first talking to your doctor or pharmacist. Do not take it with antidepressants called MAO inhibitors — this can be dangerous. It can raise your blood pressure and heart rate, so use it carefully if you have any heart or blood pressure concerns. Because it can be misused to make illegal drugs, you must show ID and sign a logbook to purchase it, and there are limits on how much you can buy. Avoid in children under 12 without medical advice.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 30 mg to 60 mg taken by mouth every 4 to 6 hours as needed, or 120 mg of the extended-release form every 12 hours. Do not take more than 240 mg in one day. Take with a full glass of water and try not to take it close to bedtime so it does not keep you awake.
